# dialog


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

A dialog keeps an LLM conversation in a Jupyter notebook. You can mix
Markdown notes, runnable code with its outputs, and prompts with their
replies. You can view, edit, diff, and version-control the conversation
with notebook tools.

The format comes from [Solveit](https://solve.it.com), where people have
used dialogs for their daily work for a couple of years. `aidialog`
makes that format available to other tools. You can read and build
dialogs, edit individual messages, and convert between dialogs and LLM
chat history.

This module defines the in-memory objects:
[`Message`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message),
[`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog),
and
[`Attachment`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#attachment).
Later modules handle `.ipynb` files and chat history conversion.

``` python
from fastcore.test import *
from fastcore.nbio import mk_display, mk_error
```

## Message types

A message has one of four types:

- `note` contains Markdown.
- `code` contains executable source and its Jupyter outputs.
- `prompt` contains a user’s request and the AI’s response.
- `raw` contains untyped text.

The file writer maps these types to notebook cells.

## Identity

Messages and attachments have string ids. A dialog uses its name as its
identifier. An object compares equal to another instance with the same
identifier, or to the identifier itself. For example, you can check
`msg in dlg.messages` or remove an attachment with
`atts.remove('img1.png')`.

[`add_id_hash`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#add_id_hash)
supplies this behavior for a class. It defines `__eq__` and `__hash__`
using one identifier attribute. Sets and dictionary keys use that same
identity.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L31"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### add_id_hash

``` python
def add_id_hash(
    cls, attr
):
```

*Adds `__eq__` and `__hash__` to a cls based on a str or int `attr` id*

These two `Type` instances have the same id, but the class doesn’t yet
compare them by id:

``` python
class Type:
    def __init__(self, id): store_attr()

atts = [Type(str(i)) for i in range(5)]
test_eq(Type('0') in atts, False)
test_eq(Type('3') == atts[3], False)
```

After
[`add_id_hash`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#add_id_hash),
matching ids imply equality. An id also compares equal to its instance.
The hash agrees with these comparisons:

``` python
add_id_hash(Type, 'id')
test_eq(Type('0') in atts, True)
test_eq(Type(10) in atts, False)
test_eq(Type('3') == atts[3], True)
test_eq('1' in atts, True)
test_eq(Type('4') == '4', True)
```

``` python
atts.remove('0')
test_eq(len(atts), 4)
atts.remove(Type('3'))
test_eq(len(atts), 3)
test_eq([o.id for o in atts], ['1','2','4'])
test_eq(len({Type(1), Type(2), Type(1)}), 2)
test_eq({Type(1):"data"}[Type(1)], "data")
```

## Message

Code outputs and AI replies use Jupyter output dictionaries in a list.
This gives rendering and serialization a common input format. Display
outputs contain `output_type`, `data`, and `metadata` fields.

[`prompt_output`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#prompt_output)
stores reply text in `data['text/markdown']`. It sets
`metadata['is_ai_res']=True` to distinguish the reply from other
displayed Markdown.
[`Message.ai_res`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message.ai_res)
retrieves that text.

A
[`Message`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message)
pairs a request with the answer from its addressee. For a prompt, those
are the user’s request and the AI’s reply. For code, they are the source
and the interpreter’s outputs. Both kinds of answer belong in `output`.

Notes address everyone who reads the dialog. Raw messages have no
addressee. The index page explains this conversation model in more
detail.

The stored fields correspond to a notebook cell: `content` for source,
`output`, `msg_type`, `id`, `attachments`, `meta`, and
`execution_count`. The `prompt` type is an extension to the notebook
cell types. Unknown metadata survives saving and loading unchanged.

A host can expose selected metadata entries as attributes through
`meta_attrs`. This dictionary maps attribute names to metadata keys.
Undeclared entries remain in `meta`.

New message ids contain four random bytes as hexadecimal text. The
constructor converts supplied ids to strings. Hosts add display prefixes
themselves, such as Solveit’s DOM `_` prefix.

`content`, `output`, and `msg_type` use `DepProp` descriptors. Assigning
output calls `clear_out_cache`. Changing the type calls it and clears
the output. The base class caches its AI rendering in `_ai_rend`.
Subclasses override the hook to clear any additional output caches.

The `dlg` attribute refers to the owning dialog.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L123"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Message

``` python
def Message(
    content:str='', # The message text: markdown, code, or a prompt's request
    output:str='', # Jupyter-style output list (code and prompt messages), or ''
    id:NoneType=None, # Message id; 4 random hex bytes if None
    msg_type:str='code', # One of `smsg_types`: code, note, prompt, or raw
    attachments:NoneType=None, # `Attachment`s carried by the message
    meta:NoneType=None, # Remaining cell metadata, carried verbatim through save/load
    execution_count:NoneType=None, # A code cell's execution count, carried through save/load
    **xtras
):
```

*An ipynb cell, or Solveit message (which adds the `prompt` type)*

Factories use `Dialog.msg_cls` to choose the message class. Set it on a
[`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog)
subclass to create your own
[`Message`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message)
subclass through inherited factory methods. `read_ipynb(cls=...)` also
accepts a dialog subclass when loading a file.

The displays below show message content, outputs, and flags.

Assign a reply string to
[`Message.output`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message.output)
to convert it with
[`prompt_output`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#prompt_output).
Notebook MIME values accept either strings or lists of lines. `ai_res`
returns one string from either representation for use in chat history.

``` python
pm = Message('q', msg_type=sprompt, output='A reply')
test_eq(pm.ai_res, 'A reply')
pm.output = 'Edited reply'
test_eq(pm.output, prompt_output('Edited reply'))
test_eq(pm.ai_res, 'Edited reply')
pm_lines = Message('q', msg_type=sprompt, output=prompt_output(['Line 1\n', 'Line 2']))
test_eq(pm_lines.ai_res, 'Line 1\nLine 2')
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L210"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Message.preview

``` python
def preview(
    maxlen:int=180, # Maximum characters per line (None: no limit)
    sep:str=':', # Separator before the content; a find shows `-` on context rows
):
```

*Escaped summary rows: `id:t[directives]:content` (t: c=code n=note
p=prompt r=raw; the bracket shows meta-form nbdev directives, as in
nbio’s `CellRow`), plus a `>` line for a prompt’s reply; a contentless
tagged raw shows its `<kind>` instead. A cut row ends with the count of
characters missing*

[`Msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#msgs)
displays each message with `preview`. The row contains its id,
one-letter type, and an escaped preview of its content. A prompt’s reply
follows on a separate `>` line.

Truncated rows end with the missing character count. You can judge how
much text remains before fetching it. `summ` also limits content and
output length for dialog displays. Large outputs don’t fill the display:

A message’s rich display uses `preview`:

``` python
m = Message('in', output='out', msg_type=snote)
m
```

45d32a38:n:in ⇒ out(3)

``` python
pv = pm.preview()
test_eq(pv, f'{pm.id}:p:q\n> Edited reply')  # the reply is a line of its own, not a count
big = Message('x=1', msg_type=scode, output=code_output('y'*500))
assert 'out(' in big.preview() and len(big.summ) < 200
long_note = Message('z'*300, msg_type=snote).preview(80)
test_eq(len(long_note), 80)
assert '[300]:' not in long_note and long_note.endswith('…[237]')
assert Message('z'*300, msg_type=snote).preview(None).endswith('z'*300)  # None shows it all
tagged = Message('', msg_type=sraw, meta=dict(rec_kind='system:compact_boundary'))
test_eq(tagged.preview(), f'{tagged.id}:r:<system:compact_boundary>')  # a contentless tagged raw shows its kind
dd = Dialog(name='t', messages=[pm, big])
assert isinstance(dd.messages, Msgs)
test_eq(str(dd.messages.show(rows=1)).count('\n'), 2)  # a prompt row is two lines, plus the "more" marker
dd.messages.show()
```

    f02b9ae1:p:q
    > Edited reply
    a3a97bdd:c:x=1 ⇒ out(601)

`update` assigns attributes in one call. It ignores `UNSET` values,
which route handlers and edit operations use for fields the user hasn’t
changed.

## Building dialogs

Use `mk_message` to create and insert a message through `msg_cls`. It
appends by default. Set `idx=0` to insert at the start, or use `before`
or `after` with a message or its id:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L252"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Dialog.mk_message

``` python
def mk_message(
    content:str, *, idx:int=-1, # Insert position; -1 appends
    after:NoneType=None, # Insert after this `Message` or id
    before:NoneType=None, # Insert before this `Message` or id
    msg_type:str='code', # One of `smsg_types`
    output:str='', # Output list; code messages also accept a JSON string
    meta:NoneType=None, # Cell metadata, carried verbatim through save/load
    export:bool=False, # Also set the meta `nbdev` export flag? (`meta_exported`)
):
```

*Create and insert a message, appending by default*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L225"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### BaseDialog.mk_message

``` python
def mk_message(
    content:str, # Message text
    idx:int=-1, # Insert position; -1 appends
    after:NoneType=None, # Insert after this `Message` or id
    before:NoneType=None, # Insert before this `Message` or id
    msg_type:str='code', # One of `smsg_types`
    output:str='', # Output list; code messages also accept a JSON string
    meta:NoneType=None, # Cell metadata, carried verbatim through save/load
    export:bool=False, # Also set the meta `nbdev` export flag? (`meta_exported`)
    **kwargs
):
```

*Create and insert a message, appending by default*

``` python
dlg = Dialog(name='test')
msg = dlg.mk_message(content='1')
dlg.mk_message(content='0', before=msg) # 0 before 1
dlg.mk_message(content='2', after=msg) # 2 after 1
assert L(dlg.messages).attrgot('content') == ['0','1','2']
test_eq(len(dlg), 3)
test_eq([m.content for m in dlg], ['0','1','2'])
test_is(dlg[1], msg)
test_eq(dlg[:2], dlg.messages[:2])
```

Both
[`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog)
and [`Msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#msgs)
accept positional indexes, exact ids, and unique id prefixes. Missing
and ambiguous ids raise `KeyError` with an explanation. Find-result
collections accept ids only, never positions:

``` python
ad = Dialog(name='access', messages=[Message('a', id='aa112233'), Message('b', id='bb445566')])
test_eq(ad['bb44'].content, 'b')
test_eq(ad.messages['aa112233'].content, 'a')
with expect_fail(KeyError, 'no message id'): ad['cc']
ad['bb445566']
```

bb445566:c:b

Pass `output` when creating a message to give it an existing result.
Here
[`code_output`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#code_output)
constructs an example result:

``` python
out = code_output('64')
test_msg = dlg.mk_message('8*8', output=out)
test_eq(test_msg.output, out)
test_msg
```

6acf494f:c:8\*8 ⇒ out(103)

``` python
random.seed(42)
rd = Dialog(name='reseed')
m1 = rd.mk_message('a')
random.seed(42)
assert rd.mk_message('b').id != m1.id  # generated ids stay unique even if the global random stream is re-seeded
```


*Make new messages and insert them sequentially into the notebook
after/before a specific message.*

Copy the first two messages, then paste after the second:

``` python
dlg = Dialog(name='copy_paste')
for i in '123': dlg.mk_message(i, msg_type=snote)
def _contents(dlg): return [m.content for m in dlg.messages]
clipboard = copy.copy(dlg.messages[:2])
dlg.mk_messages(clipboard, after=dlg.messages[1])
test_eq(_contents(dlg), ['1', '2', '1', '2', '3'])
```

<a

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Message.insert_after

``` python
def insert_after(
    msgs
):
```

``` python
dlg = Dialog(name='test')
msg1,msg2,msg3 = [dlg.mk_message(o) for o in ('first','second','third')]
msg1.insert_after([Message('inserted1'), Message('inserted2')])
test_eq([m.content for m in dlg.messages], ['first', 'inserted1', 'inserted2', 'second', 'third'])
```

[`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog) is
a
[`BaseDialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#basedialog)
plus a stored `dlg` on each message. From a message in a loaded dialog,
`m.dlg.save()` saves that dialog.

``` python
d2 = Dialog(name='test2', messages=[Message('a'), Message('b')])
assert all(m.dlg is d2 for m in d2.messages)
b2 = BaseDialog(name='base', messages=[Message('a')])
assert b2.mk_message('b').dlg is None and b2.messages[0].dlg is None
```

## Sections

A Markdown heading at the start of a note begins a section. The section
ends before the next heading at the same or a higher level.

[`header_info`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#header_info)
returns the heading’s `(level, text)` from the start of the content. It
accepts up to three leading spaces, as CommonMark allows. Hosts use this
helper for sections, collapsing, and outlines.
[`Message.header_level`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message.header_level)
returns zero unless the message is a note starting with a heading.

`section_msgs(ms, head)` returns the heading and the messages in its
section. Pass the collection to search as `ms`. For example, a host can
exclude skipped messages before finding a section. The function respects
that filtered collection rather than using `dlg.messages`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L322"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

*Markdown heading (level, text) of `content`’s first line; (0, None) if
not a heading*

``` python
sd = Dialog(name='sect')
h1,a,h2,b,h3 = [sd.mk_message(c, msg_type=t) for c,t in
    [('# Top',snote),('body',snote),('## Sub\ndetail below',snote),('x=1',scode),('# Next',snote)]]
test_eq([m.header_level() for m in sd.messages], [1,0,2,0,1])
test_eq(sd.mk_message('#not a heading', msg_type=snote).header_level(), 0)  # markdown needs the space
test_eq(header_info('## Sub  \nmore'), (2, 'Sub  '))  # (level, text) of the first line
test_eq(header_info('  ## Indented'), (2, 'Indented'))  # CommonMark allows up to 3 leading spaces
test_eq(header_info('    ## Code'), (0, None))  # 4+ spaces is an indented code block, not a heading
test_eq(sd.mk_message('   # Deep', msg_type=snote).header_level(), 1)
test_eq(section_msgs(sd.messages, h1), [h1,a,h2,b])  # stops before the next same-or-higher heading
test_eq(section_msgs(sd.messages, h2), [h2,b])  # body text under the heading doesn't change its level
test_eq(section_msgs(sd.messages, a), [a])  # a non-heading has no span
```

``` python
err_out = [dict(output_type='error', ename='ZeroDivisionError', evalue='division by zero', traceback=[])]
test_eq(Message('1/0', msg_type=scode, output=err_out).has_error, True)
```

Display and result outputs can contain Markdown. Stream outputs, such as
prints, cannot:

``` python
out_stream = [dict(output_type='stream', name='stdout', text='plain\n')]
out_display = [dict(output_type='display_data', metadata={}, data={'text/markdown': '*hi*'})]
out_exec = [dict(output_type='execute_result', metadata={}, data={'text/markdown': '**lo**'}, execution_count=1)]
test_eq(get_output_mds(out_stream), [])
test_eq(get_output_mds(out_display + out_exec), ['*hi*', '**lo**'])
test_eq(get_output_mds(None), [])
```

## Rendering outputs for the AI

[`render_outputs_ai`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#render_outputs_ai)
converts Jupyter outputs to text for the model. It combines streams as a
terminal would display them and removes ANSI codes. It prefers Markdown
to HTML. Images don’t appear in this text because chat history sends
them separately as media parts.

The renderer uses `preferred_msg_out`, `concat_streams`, and `join_out`
from `fastcore.nbio`. Below,
[`Message.render_out`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message.render_out)
caches the result. Hosts can customize individual MIME conversions
through `Message.ai_renderers`.

`AI_RENDERERS` defines the conversion for each preferred MIME type. It
removes ANSI codes from plain text, normalizes LaTeX delimiters, and
wraps JavaScript in `<script>` tags.

[`render_output_ai`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#render_output_ai)
handles one output.
[`render_outputs_ai`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#render_outputs_ai)
handles a list. Both use `preferred_msg_out` to select a MIME
representation. Pass `renderers` to override or extend the conversion
table for one call. Pass `dollars=True` for consumers that need
dollar-delimited math.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L354"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### normalize_text_latex

``` python
def normalize_text_latex(
    s:str, dollars:bool=False
):
```

*Canonicalize a `text/latex` payload to `\(...\)`/`\[...\]` delimiters,
or `$...$`/`$$...$$` with `dollars`*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L376"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### render_outputs_ai

``` python
def render_outputs_ai(
    outputs, renderers:NoneType=None, dollars:bool=False
):
```

*Plain-text rendering of a Jupyter output list for LLM context*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L370"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### render_output_ai

``` python
def render_output_ai(
    out, renderers:NoneType=None, dollars:bool=False
):
```

*Plain-text rendering of one Jupyter output, as the AI sees it;
`renderers` overrides/extends the per-mime table and `dollars` picks
`$`-spelled math*

A carriage return overwrites earlier stream text, as it would in a
terminal. An error contributes its traceback:

``` python
test_eq(render_outputs_ai([{'output_type': 'stream', 'name': 'stdout', 'text': 'Hello\rBye\n'}]), 'Bye\n')  # chkstyle: ignore
test_eq(render_output_ai({'output_type': 'execute_result', 'data': {'text/plain': '"42"'}}), '"42"')
test_eq(render_output_ai({'output_type': 'display_data', 'data': {'text/markdown': '**bold**'}}), '**bold**')
test_eq(render_output_ai({'output_type': 'display_data', 'data': {'text/latex': '$x^2$'}}, renderers={'text/latex': str.upper}), '$X^2$')
test_eq(render_output_ai({'output_type': 'error', 'traceback': ['Error: something broke']}), 'Error: something broke')
test_eq(render_output_ai({'output_type': 'display_data', 'data': {'text/html': '<b>hi</b>', 'text/plain': 'hi'}}), '<b>hi</b>')
assert not render_output_ai({'output_type': 'execute_result', 'data': {'text/plain': ''}})
```

Models tend to repeat the math delimiters in their context.
[`normalize_text_latex`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#normalize_text_latex)
gives `text/latex` outputs consistent delimiters. It accepts bare TeX
and the usual inline and display wrappers. By default, the result uses
`\(...\)` for inline math and `\[...\]` for display math:

``` python
def _tl(s, expected, dollars=False): test_eq(normalize_text_latex(s, dollars=dollars), expected)
_tl(r'\(x + y\)', r'\(x + y\)')
_tl(r'$$x + y$$', r'\[x + y\]')
_tl(r'$x + y$', r'\(x + y\)')
_tl(r'x^2 + y^2', r'\(x^2 + y^2\)')
_tl(r'$$\begin{align}x &= 1\\y &= 2\end{align}$$', r'\[\begin{align}x &= 1\\y &= 2\end{align}\]')
_tl(r'\text{Price is: \$5.00}', r'\(\text{Price is: \$5.00}\)')
_tl(r'\begin{align}E = mc^2\end{align}', r'\[\begin{align}E = mc^2\end{align}\]')
```

For apps whose users write dollar-delimited math, pass `dollars=True`.
Escaped dollars inside the expression remain unchanged. The output
rendering functions accept both `dollars` and `renderers`:

``` python
_tl(r'\(x + y\)', r'$x + y$', dollars=True)
_tl(r'\[x + y\]', r'$$x + y$$', dollars=True)
_tl(r'$x + y$', r'$x + y$', dollars=True)
_tl(r'\begin{align}E = mc^2\end{align}', r'$$\begin{align}E = mc^2\end{align}$$', dollars=True)
_tl(r'\text{Price is: \$5.00}', r'$\text{Price is: \$5.00}$', dollars=True)
test_eq(render_output_ai({'output_type': 'display_data', 'data': {'text/latex': '$x^2$'}}), r'\(x^2\)')
test_eq(render_output_ai({'output_type': 'display_data', 'data': {'text/latex': ['$x^', '2$']}}), r'\(x^2\)')
test_eq(render_output_ai({'output_type': 'display_data', 'data': {'text/latex': r'\(x^2\)'}}, dollars=True), '$x^2$')
test_eq(render_outputs_ai([{'output_type': 'display_data', 'data': {'text/latex': '$$x$$'}}], dollars=True), '$$x$$')
```

The default `text/plain` renderer joins lists of lines from notebook
files and removes ANSI codes. A per-call `renderers` entry replaces that
conversion:

``` python
def _res(data): return {'output_type': 'execute_result', 'data': data}
test_eq(render_output_ai(_res({'text/plain': ['\x1b[31mred\x1b[0m']})), 'red')
test_eq(render_output_ai(_res({'text/plain': '\x1b[31mred\x1b[0m'})), 'red')
test_eq(render_output_ai(_res({'text/plain': ['42']}), renderers={'text/plain': lambda d: f'<{d}>'}), "<['42']>")
outs = [{'output_type': 'stream', 'name': 'stdout', 'text': 'a\n'}, {'output_type': 'stream', 'name': 'stdout', 'text': 'b\n'}, _res({'text/plain': ['42']})]
render_outputs_ai(outs)
```

    'a\nb\n\n42'

[`render_md`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#render_md)
converts output lists to Markdown for documents such as aihist’s
`dlg2md` exports. Consecutive text outputs share an `output` code fence.
Markdown and LaTeX appear directly in the document. Raster images use
data-URI links. SVG uses a raw HTML fence instead.

HTML uses a Pandoc `{=html}` raw fence. Use a Pandoc-compatible
processor for this format. GFM renderers display the fence as a code
block. HTML takes precedence by default because it usually contains the
richest representation. Pass `html1st=False` to prefer Markdown.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L397"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### render_md

``` python
def render_md(
    outputs, html1st:bool=True
):
```

*Render notebook outputs as Markdown: text to \`\`fences, HTML in\`,
markdown inlined, images as data URIs*

``` python
outs = [{'output_type': 'stream', 'name': 'stdout', 'text': 'hello world\n'}, {'output_type': 'stream', 'name': 'stderr', 'text': 'warn\n'}, _res({'text/plain': ['42']})]
print(render_md(outs))
```

    ```output
    hello world
    warn
    42
    ```

``` python
disp = [mk_display(text_html=['<b>42</b>'], text_markdown=['**42**'], text_plain=['42'])]
test_eq(render_md(disp), fenced('<b>42</b>', '{=html}'))
test_eq(render_md(disp, html1st=False), '**42**')

test_eq(render_md([mk_display(image_png='abc')]), '![](data:image/png;base64,abc)')
test_eq(render_md([mk_error('oops')]), fenced('oops', 'output'))
test_eq(render_md([{'output_type': 'stream', 'name': 'stdout', 'text': 'a `` b\n'}]), '```output\na `` b\n```')
```

## Kernel outputs

A running kernel sends results as iopub messages.
[`fastcore.nbio.msg2out`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/nbio.html#msg2out)
converts these to the notebook output dictionaries that
[`Message`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message)
stores. It performs the conversion of `nbformat.v4.output_from_msg`
without requiring `nbformat`.

The
[`mk_jmsg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#mk_jmsg)
helpers construct messages for tests and for hosts that need to generate
outputs themselves.

``` python
test_eq(msg2out(mk_stream('hi\n')), dict(output_type='stream', name='stdout', text='hi\n'))
test_eq(msg2out(mk_execresult({'text/plain':'2'}))['execution_count'], 1)

with expect_fail(ValueError, 'Unrecognized'): msg2out(mk_jmsg('status'))
```

Call `add_output` for each incoming kernel message. It converts the
message to an output dictionary and updates the stored outputs.

After `clear_output(wait=True)`, the next call to `add_output` clears
the previous outputs. A trailing semicolon in the source suppresses
`execute_result`. A display-id update replaces the earlier output with
that id.

Hosts can customize handling through callbacks. `trunc` transforms each
new output dictionary, for example to truncate it. `on_input` receives
`input_request` messages, for example to display an input form. Neither
callback requires overriding the method.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L470"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Message.add_output

``` python
def add_output(
    jmsg, # A Jupyter iopub message dict
    trunc:NoneType=None, # Optional transform applied to each new output dict, e.g. truncation
    on_input:NoneType=None, # Optional handler for kernel `input_request` messages
):
```

*Convert iopub message `jmsg` to an output dict and add it to this
message’s outputs*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L464"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Message.clear_output

``` python
def clear_output(
    wait:bool=False
):
```

*Clear outputs now, or on the next `add_output` if `wait`*

``` python
km = Message('1+1', msg_type=scode, output=[])
km.add_output(mk_stream('hi\n'))
km.add_output(mk_execresult({'text/plain':'2'}))
test_eq([o['output_type'] for o in km.output], ['stream','execute_result'])
km.clear_output(wait=True)
test_eq(len(km.output), 2)  # nothing cleared yet
km.add_output(mk_stream('fresh\n'))
test_eq([o['text'] for o in km.output], ['fresh\n'])  # the pending clear ran first
test_eq(Message('2+2;', msg_type=scode, output=[]).add_output(mk_execresult({'text/plain':'4'})), None)  # semicolon suppresses
```

Updating a display id does not mutate the incoming kernel message. Here
`trunc` shortens an output and `on_input` records an input request:

``` python
dm = Message('show', msg_type=scode, output=[])
dm.add_output(mk_dispdata({'text/plain':'v1'}, display_id='d1'))
upd = mk_jmsg('update_display_data', data={'text/plain':'v2'}, transient={'display_id':'d1'})
dm.add_output(upd)
test_eq(upd['header']['msg_type'], 'update_display_data')
test_eq([o['data']['text/plain'] for o in dm.output], ['v2'])  # updated in place
seen = []
dm.add_output(mk_stream('x'*10), trunc=lambda o: o | dict(text=o['text'][:4]))
test_eq(dm.output[-1]['text'], 'xxxx')
dm.add_output(mk_jmsg('input_request', prompt='Name?', password=False), on_input=seen.append)
test_eq(seen[0]['content']['prompt'], 'Name?')
```

## Exported code

A message can declare nbdev export in its source with `#| export`, or in
its metadata under `meta['nbdev']`. The read-only `exported` property
checks both forms. `directives` combines source and metadata directives
using nbdev’s rule: source comments take precedence.

Users edit source directives as text. Hosts can read or assign
`meta_exported` to control the metadata form independently. Assigning
`meta_exported` never changes source text.

[`dlg2py`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dlg2py)
joins the exported code messages into a Python source string for
export-to-file features.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L520"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>


target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Message.directive

``` python
def directive(
    name, default:NoneType=None

```

*Value of directive `name` (`''` if bare), or `default` if absent*

``` python
em = Message('#| eval: false\n1+1')
test_eq(em.directive('eval'), 'false')
assert em.has_directive('eval') and not em.has_directive('export')
Message('#| export\nx=1').directive('export')
```

    ''

``` python
xd = Dialog(name='exp')
e1 = xd.mk_message('#| export\ndef f(): pass', msg_type=scode)
e2 = xd.mk_message('def g(): pass', msg_type=scode)
e3 = xd.mk_message('def h(): pass', msg_type=scode, meta={'nbdev': {'export': 'true'}})
xd.mk_message('#| export\nexported note', msg_type=snote)
test_eq([m.exported for m in xd.messages], [True, False, True, True])  # comment, none, meta, comment
test_eq([m.meta_exported for m in xd.messages], [False, False, True, False])  # the switch sees only meta
test_eq(e1.directives, {'export': ''})
e2.meta_exported = True  # the switch writes meta, not content
test_eq((e2.content, e2.meta), ('def g(): pass', {'nbdev': {'export': 'true'}}))
test_eq(dlg2py(xd), '#| export\ndef f(): pass\n\ndef g(): pass\n\ndef h(): pass')  # code only
e2.meta_exported = False  # off clears meta only
test_eq((e2.exported, e2.meta), (False, {}))
e1.meta_exported = True  # a comment-exported message gains the meta form too; content untouched
test_eq((e1.content, e1.meta), ('#| export\ndef f(): pass', {'nbdev': {'export': 'true'}}))
e1.meta_exported = False  # still exported: the comment is text the user owns
test_eq((e1.exported, e1.meta_exported, e1.content, e1.meta), (True, False, '#| export\ndef f(): pass', {}))
```

A summary marks metadata directives as `t[directives]`, matching nbio’s
`CellRow`. Source directives need no extra marker because the preview
already shows them:

``` python
test_eq(e3.preview(), f'{e3.id}:c[export]:def h(): pass')
test_eq(e1.preview(maxlen=200), f'{e1.id}:c:#| export¶def f(): pass')
```

``` python
em = xd.mk_message('def k(): pass', msg_type=scode, export=True)
test_eq((em.meta_exported, em.meta), (True, {'nbdev': {'export': 'true'}}))
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L537"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Message.update

``` python
def update(
    mergemeta:dict=None, # `deep_merge` into `meta`; a `None` value deletes its key
    export:bool=None, # Add (True) or remove (False) the nbdev export directive; a content-form line migrates to meta
    **kwargs
):
```

*Update this message’s attributes; returns self*

Use `update(mergemeta=...)` to deep-merge metadata. A `None` value
deletes its key. Use `export=True` to add export or `export=False` to
remove it. There is no negative export directive.

The `export` argument removes a source export line and sets the metadata
flag. It preserves only the flag from a valued directive such as
`#| export: mod`, not the module value.

You can assign ordinary attributes in the same call. An unknown
attribute name raises `AttributeError`. Use `mergemeta` for custom
metadata rather than assigning undeclared attributes:

``` python
um = Message('#| export\ndef h(): pass', msg_type=scode)
um.update(export=True)
test_eq((um.content, um.meta_exported), ('def h(): pass', True))  # content-form line migrated to meta
um.update(export=False, mergemeta=dict(k=dict(a=1)), content='def h2(): pass')
test_eq((um.content, um.meta, um.exported), ('def h2(): pass', {'k': {'a': 1}}, False))
um.update(meta={}).meta
```

    {}

``` python
test_fail(lambda: um.update(i_colapsed=True), contains='i_colapsed')  # typo'd or undeclared fields fail loudly
```

Splitting a message preserves its export status in each piece. Splitting
already copies metadata, including metadata export directives. For a
source directive,
[`copy_export`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#copy_export)
copies the leading line with its spelling and value intact. It does not
prepend a directive when the destination already starts with `#|`. Both
aidialog and Solveit use it in
[`split_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#split_msg).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L560"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### copy_export

``` python
def copy_export(
    s, src
):
```

*Prepend `src`’s leading export directive line to `s`, unless `s`
already starts with a `#|` directive*

``` python
test_eq(copy_export('def g(): pass', '#|exports: mymod\ndef f(): pass'), '#|exports: mymod\ndef g(): pass')
test_eq(copy_export('#| hide\nx', '#| export\ny'), '#| hide\nx')  # a piece with its own directive is left alone
test_eq(copy_export('def g(): pass', 'def f(): pass'), 'def g(): pass')
```

`merge_content` prepares a message for a merge into the requested target
type. A code target takes the source unchanged. A note target includes a
prompt’s request and response as sections, and code inside a fence.
Hosts can override the method for their own formatting conventions.
`aidialog.merge_msgs` calls it when merging messages:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L567"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Message.merge_content

``` python
def merge_content(
    mtype:str, # The merge target's msg_type
):
```

*This message’s content contribution when merged into a `mtype` message;
hosts override for their own conventions*

``` python
pm2 = Message('Sum?', msg_type=sprompt, output='It is 3.')
test_eq(pm2.merge_content(snote), '## AI Prompt\nSum?\n## AI Response\nIt is 3.')
test_eq(pm2.merge_content(scode), 'Sum?')
test_eq(Message('x=1', msg_type=scode).merge_content(snote), '```python\nx=1\n```')
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L589"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### merge_parts

``` python
def merge_parts(
    msgs, srcs:NoneType=None
):
```

*Merged `(content, meta)` for combining `msgs` (optionally with
per-message rendered `srcs`): later messages’ directive lines fold into
the merged meta, first message winning conflicts*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L578"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### merge_metas

``` python
def merge_metas(
    metas
):
```

*First-wins merge of cell metadata dicts, merging the `nbdev` directives
dict one level deeper*

[`merge_metas`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#merge_metas)
combines metadata dictionaries. The first value for each key wins. It
also merges the `nbdev` dictionary one level deeper. Hosts can use this
function without message objects.

[`merge_parts`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#merge_parts)
returns merged content and metadata for a list of messages. It uses each
message’s effective directives, with source comments taking precedence
over that message’s metadata. It removes directive lines from later
messages and includes their directives in the merged metadata.
Directives in the first message’s source remain there, without duplicate
metadata entries. The first message wins conflicts.

[`merge_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#merge_msgs)
and host merge implementations use these helpers:

``` python
ma = Message('#| export\ndef a(): pass', msg_type=scode)
mb = Message('#| export\ndef b(): pass', msg_type=scode, meta={'nbdev': {'eval': 'false'}, 'k': 1})
mc = Message('def c(): pass', msg_type=scode, meta={'k': 2})
test_eq(merge_metas([mb.meta, mc.meta]), {'nbdev': {'eval': 'false'}, 'k': 1})
c,meta = merge_parts([ma,mb,mc])
test_eq(c, '#| export\ndef a(): pass\n\ndef b(): pass\n\ndef c(): pass')
test_eq(meta, {'k': 1, 'nbdev': {'eval': 'false'}})  # export stays as ma's comment line; mb's eval folds in
c2,meta2 = merge_parts([mc,ma])  # an exported later piece exports the merge, via meta
test_eq((c2, meta2), ('def c(): pass\n\ndef a(): pass', {'k': 2, 'nbdev': {'export': 'true'}}))
```

## Validation

Direct attribute assignment can leave a message with malformed outputs
or metadata that JSON cannot serialize. A dialog can also contain
duplicate ids. Call `validate` to check these conditions before saving.
It raises `ValueError` with the offending message or dialog-level
problem. It never repairs the data.

These checks cover the in-memory model.
[`fastcore.nbio.validate_nb`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/nbio.html#validate_nb)
checks notebook file structure.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L604"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Message.validate

``` python
def validate():
```

*Raise `ValueError` for problems that would break saving or rendering;
returns self if fine*

``` python
test_eq(Message('1+1', id=1, msg_type=scode, output=[]).validate().id, '1')  # ids coerce to str at construction
m = Message('1+1', msg_type=scode, output=code_output('2'))
test_eq(m.validate(), m)
m.output = [dict(no_type=1)]
with expect_fail(ValueError, 'bad output entry'): m.validate()
with expect_fail(ValueError, 'must not carry output'): Message('n', msg_type=snote, output='x').validate()
with expect_fail(ValueError, 'not JSON-serializable'): Message('m', msg_type=snote, meta=dict(x={1,2})).validate()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L621"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Dialog.validate

``` python
def validate():
```

*Validate every message plus dialog-scope rules (unique ids,
serializable `meta`); returns self if fine*

``` python
vd = Dialog(name='v', messages=[Message('a', msg_type=snote), Message('b', msg_type=snote)])
test_eq(vd.validate(), vd)
vd.messages.append(Message('c', msg_type=snote, id=vd.messages[0].id))
with expect_fail(ValueError, 'duplicate message id'): vd.validate()
```

## Attachments

An
[`Attachment`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#attachment)
stores named binary data, usually an image, on a message. File
serialization uses the standard Jupyter attachments dictionary.
Generated ids use UUID4 format.
[`ruuid4`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#ruuid4)
uses `rtoken_hex` and the seeded `random` generator for reproducible
test ids.

`tiny_png` is a minimal valid one-pixel PNG, exported for examples and

Copy/paste keeps attachments with their messages:

``` python
test_eq(Attachment(b'x', 'text/plain', id=42).id, '42')  # ids coerce to str at construction
dlg_attach = Dialog(name='attach_test')
att1 = Attachment(data=b'screenshot1', content_type='image/png', id='img1.png')
m1 = dlg_attach.mk_message('1. Message with screenshot', msg_type=snote, attachments=[att1])
m2 = dlg_attach.mk_message('2. No attachment', msg_type=snote)
pasted = dlg_attach.mk_messages(copy.copy(dlg_attach.messages[:1]), after=m2)
test_eq(len(dlg_attach.messages), 3)
test_eq(pasted[0].attachments[0].id, 'img1.png')
test_eq(pasted[0].attachments[0].data, b'screenshot1')
```

## Splitting messages

[`Message.split`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message.split)
returns detached parts when the message has no dialog. For a message in
a dialog, it inserts the new parts after the original. The first part
keeps the original message and its output.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L658"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Message.split

``` python
def split(
    *linenos:int, # Split before each of these 1-based lines
):
```

*Split this message into pieces (returned as
[`Msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#msgs); the
first keeps its id): one `'\n\n'` is absorbed at each cut (so
[`merge_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#merge_msgs)
restores blank-line-separated content byte-exactly), `meta_attrs`
fields, the cell `meta`, and a leading `#| export` copy to every piece,
attachments follow their references, and unreferenced ones stay on the
first piece*

``` python
parts = Message('one\ntwo').split(2)
test_eq([m.content for m in parts], ['one', 'two'])
assert all(m.dlg is None for m in parts)
```

*Public stored fields plus the derived `exported` flag, with `output` as

[`Message.todict`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message.todict)
returns a dictionary for hosts. It omits private fields and attachments.
It replaces `output` with the AI text rendering and includes the derived
`exported` flag. Hosts don’t need to recompute that flag from source and
metadata.

``` python
m = Message('#| export\ndef f(): pass', msg_type=scode)
test_eq(m.todict()['exported'], True)
test_eq(Message('1+1', msg_type=scode).todict()['exported'], False)
mm = Message('1+1', msg_type=scode)
mm.meta['nbdev'] = {'export': 'true'}
test_eq(mm.todict()['exported'], True)
```

## XML views

The editing toolkit reads messages and dialogs as concise XML using
`item2xml`’s grammar. Each message’s type tag contains its content
directly. An `<out>` section contains a code output or prompt reply.
Metadata nbdev directives become attributes.

Use
[`Message.view`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message.view)
for a line-oriented display instead. It can include line numbers or
exhash addresses.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L712"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
vm = Message('x = 1\nx', output=code_output('1'))
```

    1: x = 1
    2: x
    <out>
    1
    </out>

Read-only notebook tools can also read dialogs.
[`Message.source`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message.source)
exposes its content and
[`Message.cell_type`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message.cell_type)
reports the type that `to_cell` writes. `Dialog.cells` exposes the
messages as cells for consumers such as `nb_frontmatter`.

A prompt serializes as a code cell. Its `cell_type` therefore reports
`code`, even though its content isn’t executable Python. Execution must
check `msg_type` instead. `select_msgs` below makes that distinction.

## Running a dialog

[`Dialog.execute`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog.execute)
runs code messages in an execnb `CaptureShell`. It stores the resulting
notebook-format outputs on each message in memory. Call `save`
explicitly to write them to disk, as with other session operations.

[`Dialog.select_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog.select_msgs)
chooses what to run. It uses
[`fastcore.nbio.select_cells`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/nbio.html#select_cells)
for ids, unique prefixes, and `above` and `below` anchors. It then keeps
only messages whose `msg_type` is `code`. Prompts never execute, even
though they serialize as code cells.

For messages other than explicit id selections, the cell’s `eval`
directive determines participation. Without that directive, selection
uses the notebook’s setting, then `default_eval`. Pass
`ignore_eval=True` to skip this filtering. Explicitly selected code
messages run regardless of `eval`.

`d.execute(m.id, above=True)` runs the selected code through `m`,
inclusive. With no arguments, `d.execute()` runs all participating code
messages, like Solveit’s run-all.

The returned
[`RunResult`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#runresult)
contains the messages that ran and displays their status. You can look
up messages by id.

Long reports collapse successful lines into counted markers. The report
keeps the lines nearest the selection anchor: the last lines for an
`above` run, or the first for a `below` run. Failures always appear with
their exception name and value. The final line counts successes and
failures, as `%nbrun` does.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L768"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### RunResult

``` python
def RunResult(
    items:NoneType=None, head:bool=False
):
```

*Messages run by
[`Dialog.execute`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog.execute),
shown as a status report*

Without a `shell` argument, each execution call creates its own
`CaptureShell`. Later calls do not reuse that namespace. Pass your own
shell to retain variables across calls.

Every message that runs gets new outputs, including failures that
replace earlier successful results. Messages that the run never reaches
keep their previous outputs.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L808"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Dialog.execute

``` python
def execute(
    *ids, # Message ids, or unique prefixes, to run; with `above`/`below`, the anchor; none, with no selection flags: run all
    shell:NoneType=None, # `CaptureShell` to run in, kept for the caller; default is a fresh one, dropped at the end
    continue_on_error:bool=False, # Keep running after a failure?
    timeout:int=None, # Seconds before each message's run times out
    above:bool=False, # Include each matched cell and all cells above it?
    below:bool=False, # Include each matched cell and all cells below it?
    all:bool=False, # Include all code cells (ignores `msgids`)?
    exported:bool=False, # Only cells with `#| export` or `#| exports`?
    default_eval:bool=True, # Participation default when neither the cell nor the notebook has an `eval` directive
    ignore_eval:bool=False, # Skip `eval` filtering entirely: every selected cell runs
):
```

*Run code messages on an execnb `CaptureShell`, capturing outputs into
each message, and return a
[`RunResult`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#runresult)
status report; blocks (use `asyncio.to_thread` in async hosts); `save`
persists outputs*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L802"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Dialog.select_msgs

``` python
def select_msgs(
    *ids, above:bool=False, # Include each matched cell and all cells above it?
    below:bool=False, # Include each matched cell and all cells below it?
    all:bool=False, # Include all code cells (ignores `msgids`)?
    exported:bool=False, # Only cells with `#| export` or `#| exports`?
    default_eval:bool=True, # Participation default when neither the cell nor the notebook has an `eval` directive
    ignore_eval:bool=False, # Skip `eval` filtering entirely: every selected cell runs
):
```

*The messages a non-interactive run executes: `select_cells` mechanics
(ids, above/below, the eval cascade) over the notebook projection, code
messages only*

[`Message.execute`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message.execute)
runs one message with the same shell behavior. Pass a shell from an
earlier dialog run to reuse its variables.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L828"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Message.execute

``` python
def execute(
    shell:NoneType=None, # `CaptureShell` to run in, kept for the caller; default is a fresh one, dropped at the end
    timeout:int=None, # Seconds before the run times out
):
```

*Run this code message on an execnb `CaptureShell`, capturing outputs
into it*

This run executes the two code messages and skips the note and prompt:

``` python
rd = Dialog(name='runs')
r1 = rd.mk_message('y = 7')
r2 = rd.mk_message('print("hi"); y*6')
rd.mk_message('A note', msg_type=snote)
rd.mk_message('What is y?', output='7.', msg_type=sprompt)
test_eq([m.id for m in rd.select_msgs(all=True)], [r1.id, r2.id])
res = rd.execute()
test_eq(len(res), 2)
res
```

    974162d7: ok
    c2599acf: ok
    run: 2 msgs ok

The messages now hold notebook-format outputs in memory. The run has not
saved a file:

``` python
test_eq(r2.output[0]['text'], ['hi\n'])
test_eq(r2.output[1]['data']['text/plain'], ['42'])
r2.output
```

    [{'output_type': 'stream', 'name': 'stdout', 'text': ['hi\n']},
     {'data': {'text/plain': ['42']},
      'metadata': {},
      'output_type': 'execute_result',
      'execution_count': 2}]

Pass a `CaptureShell` to both calls to reuse the namespace. The new
message can then read `y` from the dialog run:

``` python
from execnb.shell import CaptureShell
```

``` python
sh = CaptureShell()
rd.execute(shell=sh)
nm = rd.mk_message('y+1')
res = nm.execute(shell=sh)
test_eq(nm.output[0]['data']['text/plain'], ['8'])
res
```

    44eda2e2: ok
    run: 1 msg ok

Without that shell, the new message has no `y`. Execution captures the
`NameError` in the message’s outputs and reports the failure:

``` python
res = nm.execute()
assert nm.has_error
res
```

    44eda2e2: NameError: name 'y' is not defined
    run: 0 msgs ok, 1 failed

By default, execution stops at the first failure. The messages after it
retain their previous outputs:

``` python
bad = rd.mk_message('1/0', after=r1.id)
res = rd.execute()
test_eq([m.id for m in res], [r1.id, bad.id])
test_eq(r2.output[1]['data']['text/plain'], ['42'])
res
```

    974162d7: ok
    dae451f3: ZeroDivisionError: division by zero
    run: 1 msg ok, 1 failed

Set `continue_on_error=True` to run past failures. The report counts
successes and failures separately:

``` python
res = rd.execute(continue_on_error=True)
test_eq(len(res), 4)
res
```

    974162d7: ok
    dae451f3: ZeroDivisionError: division by zero
    c2599acf: ok
    44eda2e2: ok
    run: 3 msgs ok, 1 failed

## Export selection

[`export_filter`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#export_filter)
selects the messages that take part when exporting document content
rather than the whole transcript, as aihist’s `dlg2md` does with
`exportfilter=True`. If any message has an export directive,
[`export_filter`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#export_filter)
selects all exported messages, including pinned ones. Otherwise it
selects all non-pinned messages. Adding the first export directive
switches between those rules.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dialog.py#L836"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### export_filter

``` python
def export_filter(
    ms
):
```

*The messages participating in an export: every exported one if any
